summary.name: Numbers: Make Spreadsheets
summary.one_liner: Apple's Numbers is a free spreadsheet app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and the web (iCloud.com) with templates, charts, pivot tables, and hundreds of formulas.
use_cases: Build a home budget or personal finance tracker
Analyze data with pivot tables and charts
Edit Excel or CSV files on iPhone, iPad, or Mac
Collaborate on a shared spreadsheet in real time
Fill out data-entry forms on a phone or tablet
summary.what_it_does: Numbers lets users create spreadsheets on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and via iCloud.com on a PC, starting from Apple-designed templates or a blank flexible canvas where tables, charts, text, and images can be placed freely. It supports hundreds of functions including XLOOKUP and RegEx, an integrated function browser, and spilling arrays. Data can be summarized with pivot tables and categories, shown in 2D and 3D charts (bar, column, line, area, pie, donut, radar, plus interactive scatter and bubble), and controlled through sliders, checkboxes, pop-ups, and star ratings. Files can be imported from and exported to Microsoft Excel and CSV, and exported also as TSV and PDF, and shared publicly or with specific people via iCloud or Box with real-time change tracking.
notable: Free to download with in-app purchases; creating, viewing, editing, and real-time collaboration do not require a subscription
Imports and edits Microsoft Excel and CSV files
Apple Intelligence features like Writing Tools and Image Playground require a compatible device
Listed as Freeware in the awesome-mac list under Office
caveats: In-app purchases include an Intelligence Usage Pack ($49.99) and Monthly ($12.99) or Annual ($129.00) plans; Apple Intelligence features need a capable device and have usage limits
Requires iOS 26.0, iPadOS 26.0, or macOS 26.0 or later
Numbers is now part of Apple Creator Studio, a bundled plan; the page lists it alongside other Apple apps
